Zaanan
ZAY-a-nan
proper noun
Hebrew Tsa'anan, likely “going out” or “place of flocks,” a town of the Judean lowland named in Micah’s lament in a pun upon its name.

📖 Biblical Definition

Zaanan means “going out,” and Micah makes a bitter wordplay of it: the town whose name is Sally-forth cannot sally forth. “The inhabitant of Zaanan came not forth in the mourning of Bethezel” (Mic 1:11). When judgment falls, the people who should march out to battle or flee to safety are paralysed, shut up within their walls, unable to move. The prophet Micah “saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem” (Mic 1:1) a doom that had come home to Judah: “it is come unto Judah; he is come unto the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem” (Mic 1:9). And over the whole ravaged land he raised the cry, “evil came down from the LORD unto the gate of Jerusalem” (Mic 1:12). Zaanan preaches the helplessness of the sinner under the hand of God. The town that lived by going out is frozen where it stands; the strength that men presume upon fails them utterly in the hour of wrath. There is a paralysis that falls upon the guilty when God arises to judge, so that they can neither fight nor flee. Only He who binds can loose; and the sinner who would go out from the prison of his guilt must wait upon the mercy of God, for no strength of his own will open the gate.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A lowland town of Judah in Micah’s lament (Mic 1:11) whose name means “going out”; unable to come forth in the day of judgment, a picture of the sinner’s helplessness under God’s hand.

ZAANAN, a town of the Judean lowland (shephelah).

Its name likely means “going out” or “place of flocks.”

Named in Micah’s lament in a pun upon its name (Mic 1:11).

Its inhabitant “came not forth” in the day of mourning.

A picture of the sinner’s paralysis under the hand of God.

📖 Key Scripture

Mic 1:11 — "the inhabitant of Zaanan came not forth in the mourning of Bethezel; he shall receive of you his standing."

Mic 1:12 — "For the inhabitant of Maroth waited carefully for good: but evil came down from the LORD unto the gate of Jerusalem."

Mic 1:1 — "The word of the LORD that came to Micah the Morasthite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem."

Mic 1:9 — "For her wound is incurable; for it is come unto Judah; he is come unto the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The town of “going out” that could not go forth; the entry recovers the sinner’s helplessness under the judging hand of God.

expand to see more

Zaanan rebukes the presumption of self-sufficiency. The town named for going out is frozen where it stands when God arises; the strength men trust in fails them utterly in the hour of wrath. The wordplay is a warning: what you boast of will betray you when the LORD lays His hand upon you.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the total helplessness of the sinner apart from grace. The age preaches human capacity, resilience, and the power to break every chain by will; but Zaanan cannot come forth. There is a bondage of guilt that no native strength can loose, a paralysis that falls upon the guilty when God judges. Only He who binds can free. The sinner who would go out from the prison-house of his sin must wait upon the mercy of God in Christ, who alone opens the gate and proclaims liberty to the captive.
